title: Edda Vasse
notes: Commander Edda Vasse, the Citizen Nexus's Symbol, and her campaign. It requires all for the buildings, the Nexus powers and the bench units her levels use, and brings only her own unit. Building her and her campaign is not choosing the Citizens' roster: every building and power she is offered is still the disposable bench.

commanders.name: Edda Vasse

round-start: On my mark. That was it.
first-contact: By the book. The new book.
raid-arrives: Late arrivals. Not on my list.
unit-lost: Close the gap. I have the name.
falls: Hold it without me. Back soon.

commanders.notes: Her unit's definition (her health, her shot, the commander flag) is still TypeScript in src/content/commanders.ts; this names it, and her. Her barks are what she says during a Battle Round, by moment (src/armies/barks.ts says what each moment is): dry, tired, decent, the officer who reads the regulation aloud, in the lore's budget of three to eight words. 'By the book. The new book.' is campaigns.md's bark for her first engagement, 'Concrete sets faster under fire.' and 'File it under victories.' are the lore's Citizen barks, and 'They touched the pyramid.' answers PERIMETER's briefing ('Do not touch the pyramid.'). She falls as ordinary business and knows the schedule: out for a round, restored the round after. When she speaks, and which line, is the view's (the Vasse's voice Experiment shows them, src/view/pulse-voice.ts); none of them explains a rule.

campaigns.title: The Citizen origin
campaigns.notes: Her campaign: its levels in the order they are played. What a level offers is everything the levels before it unlocked and its own unlocks, so the screen between levels (not built) can show what is new; each level sets its own credits. vasse-test-1 and vasse-test-2 are working names, the levels a route opens (campaign?level=vasse-test-1) while the campaign is built. ground-test, last, is a test level for one Experiment rather than a step of her story, named for what it tests.

levels.notes: PERIMETER, the campaign's first level, on the Build Phase's starter map (named in the map table, src/build/maps.ts, until maps are data too). It unlocks every building and both placeholder Nexus powers all has, one by one, so that when all grows this level keeps what it teaches. Credits: a few things and not everything; the three buildings cost 85, and a second Barracks takes a plan past 100.

mission.name: Perimeter
mission.notes: PERIMETER, mission 1, as the trigger list the runner plays: three Battle Rounds, the raid arriving in each, and the hold (campaigns.md sketches it). Played on the Build Phase's starter map, not PERIMETER's own: whether that map needs real scrolling is still an open question, and it exists only as a sketch. The regions are named for this map's landmarks, the gap in the northern ridge and the open flats to the east; a real map would carry its own. The units are the disposable fixture rosters from the first battles (Citizen troopers and marksmen, 'two squads'; Ravel runners and raiders): the campaign design decided on no new content. The raid's sizes are a first tuning, not balance: chosen against this map and the starter construct menu so that the first Pulse is a probe the starting squads can meet, the second needs something built, and the third needs most of what the level's credits buy (docs/history/reports/2026-09-30-round-loop-and-missions.md has the outcomes measured against scripted plans). Since buildings came to send their units in waves (the Commander round 5), the Barracks standing on the map sends four troopers five seconds into every round, and a plan that builds nothing holds the third round; the raid was not retuned for it. pulseTicks: thirty seconds a Pulse, as the placeholder Pulse was, time enough for a group to cross the map. seed: 0x50554c53, 'PULS', the placeholder Pulse's seed, so the first round's randomness is the one 6A was tuned on. What the Barracks and the Hatchery spawn is theirs, on their cards in all (spawns), not the mission's: the Barracks standing on the map sends its wave of troopers every round, which is what makes a second round show something the first did not. The round texts are placeholder writing in PERIMETER's register ('plain, military, correct'), inside the lore budget; the briefing and debrief written in campaigns.md are the designed ones, and the mission-cutscenes milestone is where they are shown. endText's won line is the debrief's own first sentence (campaigns.md).

regions.notes: Beside the Nexus, toward where the raid comes from: where the starting squads stand.
North of the gap in the ridge: the raid's way in.
The open flats east of the base: the second round's flank.
The player's Grid Nexus: what Corvane's last line in the intro looks at.

regions.name: the line
regions.notes: Two steps out from the muster, between the Nexus and the way the raid comes round the ridge: where the player's troops stand, a line just ahead of the base.

triggers.notes: 'Commander Vasse holds the ground with what walked out of the annex: two squads' (the briefing). She is listed first, so she takes the muster's centre with the squads around her: listed last she stood at their edge and fell in round 2 behind every Turret plan measured. She arrives once; when she falls, the rules between rounds bring her back.

Where the player's troops head, every round: the line just ahead of the base. They fight what comes within their reach and stand there when nothing does, so a building placed beside the line fights beside them, and a raid that goes round them meets the buildings. Set once; it holds every round. Chosen over the gap in the ridge, the pass and the ground before the Barracks, and measured with every place one building can go inside the build range: a plan that builds nothing still lost the last round at every strength of Vasse's aura and every health from 20 to 100, as it did before the line, and the raid needed no change. With the Barracks's troopers in a wave (the Commander round 5) it holds it, at every one of those values; the troopers head for the line as soon as they are out.

spawn.intent: Probe the line at the ridge.

triggers.notes: The intro, as round 1's Build Phase opens: Vasse's own bark, then the pre-battle exchange, every line already written in campaigns.md (mission one, in full), none new. The camera goes where each line looks: at her, at the raid on the ridge, and at the Nexus for Corvane's last. Corvane is not on the Grid; the raid speaks for them.

say.speaker: unit.citizen.vasse
say.text: By the book. The new book.

say.speaker: Corvane
say.text: Nice fence, roadmakers. We brought wire cutters.

say.speaker: unit.citizen.vasse
say.text: It is not our fence I would worry about.

say.speaker: Corvane
say.text: ...Why is your pyramid looking at me?

triggers.notes: Seven seconds in: a flank that arrives while the main group is already engaged.
The raid's own Build Phase plan for the push comes first: a den north of the ridge, its forward camp.
Listed before the hold on purpose: at the last Pulse's end both could hold, and the first win or lose in list order decides.

roundText.1: A hostile force is inbound from the ridge. Hold the perimeter.
roundText.2: They are back, and there are more. Watch the east.
roundText.3: This is the push. Hold until their schedule ends.

levels.notes: The Commander's cadence as a level: Vasse stands alone out in front, falls in round 1, sits round 2 out, and the Nexus restores her for round 3. It was built as the named scenario that proves the rule (tests/commander.test.ts pins the hash each of its rounds ends on), and is a level so the game can open it by route and her return can be played: in PERIMETER she cannot fall before round 2, so her return would come in a round 4 that does not exist. It unlocks nothing new.

mission.name: The Commander falls
mission.notes: pulseTicks: twenty seconds a round, more than the line needs to finish what kills her. seed: 0x56415353, 'VASS'.

regions.notes: Out in front of the base, alone: where the ambush finds her.
Beside the Nexus, where the line stands.

triggers.notes: Two raiders and two runners: with two raiders alone, once By the Book guarded her she fell on the round's last tick at her first health, and lived at more. With the runners she falls in round 1 at every health from 20 to 100 and every strength of her aura, and the line still finishes the raid.

levels.notes: The Ground Experiment's test level (the Commander round 6): a terminal cell is about twice as tall as it is wide, and the rules count a row like a column, so this level puts two raids the same distance from the Nexus on screen and asks which arrives first. Round 1: two raiders 12 rows above the Nexus's top edge and two 24 columns past its right edge, arriving on the same tick and both going for the Nexus first. Under the rules as they are the northern raid arrives first (with nothing built, its first blow is three seconds in and the eastern raid's nine); with rows counting double the two arrive together. Round 2 brings slingers the same two ways, so a ranged reach is seen in battle. Played on open ground (src/build/maps.ts), where both raids, the Nexus and the ground between them are on screen together at 80 x 24. It unlocks nothing new: it offers what PERIMETER unlocked, with credits for about two Turrets and a Barracks, so a Turret can be placed and its reach seen. A test level like the cadence level before it, reachable by route (campaign?level=ground-test); the playable page opens it under each Ground choice (scripts/demos/ground.json).

mission.name: Ground test
mission.notes: The race as a mission: two Battle Rounds, two raids each, and the hold. The raid is small on purpose, so the race is watched rather than lost: with nothing built, round 1 ends with the Nexus untouched and round 2 with it standing, which is also what lets a route open round 2. With four raiders each way, a plan that built nothing lost the Nexus in round 1, and with three it lost more than half of it; measured on the rules as they are. pulseTicks: thirty seconds a round, as PERIMETER's, time enough for the slower raid to arrive and the fight to finish, so no raider is left standing into the next round. seed: 0x47524e44, 'GRND'. The raid's units are the bench's, as every level's are: raiders for the race, slingers for the ranged reach.

regions.notes: The player's Grid Nexus, where it stands on open ground: columns 17 to 19, rows 15 and 16.
Beside the Nexus on the west, away from both ways in: where Vasse and the squad stand as round 1 opens, so on the first tick the Nexus, not one of them, is what each raid is nearest.

regions.name: the line
regions.notes: Just in front of the Nexus, at its north-east corner, facing both raids: where the player's troops head and hold, a melee line that meets the northern raid from below and the eastern one from the side.
Straight north of the Nexus. A group gathers round the centre, 18,3: its front row is 12 rows above the Nexus's top edge, and its raiders stand over the Nexus's three columns.

Straight east of the Nexus. A group gathers round the centre, 44,16: its front is 24 columns past the Nexus's right edge, level with the Nexus's two rows. A row is about two columns tall, so this is as far away on screen as the northern group.

triggers.notes: Vasse and three troopers, the melee line. She is listed first, so she takes the muster's centre, as in PERIMETER; she arrives once, and when she falls the rules between rounds bring her back.
Where the player's troops head, every round: the line at the Nexus's corner. The Barracks's troopers head there too, as soon as they are out.

The race: two raiders each way, on the same tick, the same distance from the Nexus on screen. Two, so each group stands square to the Nexus: the northern pair one behind the other over its columns, the eastern pair side by side level with its rows.

spawn.intent: Down from the north, for the Nexus.
In from the east, for the Nexus.

triggers.notes: Ranged, the same two ways: two slingers and two runners each. The slingers stop at their reach to shoot, so where each stops shows how far a reach goes up and across; the runners beside them go on to fight hand to hand.

roundText.1: Two raids, equally far on screen. One from the north, one from the east. Watch which arrives first.
roundText.2: Slingers now, the same two ways in. Watch where each one stops to shoot.
